region.text: the Republic of Kiribati: Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands and Banaba

ledger.note: 1979: the Gilbert Islands become independent as Kiribati: infobox 'Independence from the United Kingdom, Granted: 12 July 1979'; 'The Gilbert Islands gained independence as the Republic of Kiribati on 12 July 1979.' The state includes Banaba (added to the protectorate in 1900), the northern Line Islands (added in 1919) and the Phoenix Islands (added in 1937).

certainty.note: Island groups; borders are coasts. The page speaks of a dispute with the United States over the Phoenix and Line Islands ended by treaty; no sea boundary is drawn.

sources.title: Kiribati
sources.note: Independence 12 July 1979, area 811.19 km2, islands (Gilbert 16 atolls, Phoenix 8, Line 8 plus a reef, Banaba), Tarawa with coordinates, Banaba 1900, Line Islands 1919, Phoenix 1937, Japanese occupation, Treaty of Tarawa with the US (1979, ratified 1983).

notes: Written by oc-02-x. One page opened (Kiribati). The page says the United States dispute over the Phoenix and Line Islands 'was eventually resolved and they finally became part of Kiribati under the Treaty of Tarawa': 'in September, the United States relinquished all claims to the sparsely inhabited Phoenix and Line Islands, in a 1979 treaty of friendship with Kiribati (ratified in 1983)'. The islands are already inside the state's shape from its founding (the British colony held them from 1919 and 1937), so no gain event is entered; the page gives no year for the start of the American claim, so no contest span can be dated. The page gives about 1967 for institutions of internal self-rule on Tarawa (not 1971) and 'The separation entered into force on 1 January 1976' for the Ellice Islands. The Japanese occupation (Butaritari, Tarawa and other northern Gilberts 1941 to 1943; Banaba 1942 to 1945) belongs to the pre-independence colony and is in gilbert-and-ellice-islands. The antimeridian: Kiribati straddles 180 degrees (bbox -171.64 to 174.74); the gazetteer handles the country name.
